[1/2] Make ordinary git push confirmation-gated

impact_assessment.why: The operator authorized publishing the merged main commit, but the project permission rule denies every git push and forces a manual workaround.
impact_assessment.benefits: A tested commit can be published after an explicit human confirmation; force, mirror and delete pushes remain blocked.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: git push* becomes ask, force/mirror/delete patterns stay deny; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: no state change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update opencode.jsonc and the permission-boundary test together, append ADR-265, run the unit and read-only gate shield, then push only after confirmation.

[1/1] Let Reforge repair beside unrelated uncommitted work

impact_assessment.why: Repair refused whenever any unrelated file was dirty, so a concurrent session blocked a reviewed safety fix; the user needs Reforge to fix its findings without taking over or committing another agent's work.
impact_assessment.benefits: Findings can be applied and verified while other work is in progress; only a commit whose target file was already dirty is refused, and unrelated paths are never staged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: fix/run no longer require a clean tree; dependency: none; concurrency: a fingerprint detects unrelated dirty paths changing during repair; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Snapshot and restore targets, fingerprint pre-existing unrelated paths, allow them only in the diff review, exclude them from commit_paths, and pin every case with integration tests plus an ADR.

[1/1] Show a combined rejected/duplicate row with either include flag and report full status counts

impact_assessment.why: ADR-264 described the include flags as alternatives, but a row that was both Rejected and duplicate needed both; status also used the filtered list and under-reported the register.
impact_assessment.benefits: Either flag now reveals its whole category, and status describes the register while ideas remains the working list.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a combined row appears under either flag; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Unit and CLI tests pin the combined row and the full status totals; README, architecture and ADR-267 record the semantics.

Reforge stage 2: window 10, 5 commit(s), 15 file(s) reviewed (unreviewed), 0 finding(s), 0 repaired
[1/1] Exclude prior-stage-only files from a widening review packet

impact_assessment.why: A widening stage adds one old commit and new commits, but the packet diffed the whole window and repeated the entire stage-1 refactor (201 KB) instead of reviewing only the new work.
impact_assessment.benefits: Packets are bounded by the new commits, findings cannot repeat a prior stage, and patch validation only accepts lines the new commits added.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: packet files are the union of new-commit paths; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Filter _changed_paths/_binary_paths by plan.new_shas, compute touched lines per new commit, add a unit test, and append ADR-268.

checkpoints.description: Task 'reforge-packet-scope' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: persist a fix's review status into the matching run history entry so report/status agree with last_audit

impact_assessment.why: run_pipeline fix mode updates last_audit.review and saves, but never syncs the matching history entry; after a later stage, report shows an already-reviewed stage as unreviewed, so the audit trail is wrong
impact_assessment.benefits: report and status reflect completed host reviews for every stage, history survives later stages and reloads, no schema or CLI change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: history review status becomes authoritative after fix, state schema unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: fix already holds run_lock; state: in-place update of the matching history entry then atomic save
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first test that runs fix, reloads state, and asserts history.review; full AIKit test and gate suite; ADR-269 records the invariant

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Persist a fix's reviewed status into the matching run history entry

impact_assessment.why: A fix updated last_audit.review but left the history entry unreviewed, so report contradicted the stored stage after a later stage.
impact_assessment.benefits: report, status and last_audit agree after a fix; the history survives reloads.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: history review becomes authoritative after fix; dependency: none; concurrency: fix already holds the run lock; state: in-place matching entry update, no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Call sync_last_audit before save, pin it with a failing-first unit test, append ADR-269 and run the full gate suite.
